name: cal_2x11_v5b
notes:
user notes:  hand nudged and looking good

No sweep this session — delays as imported or edited by hand. Saved 2026-08-13 18:50:26, delaycal v1.49. Sweep parameters: start 4.00 µs, coarse step 0.8 µs, fine step 40 ns, max delay 200.0 µs, averages N=32, signal detect 5.0 V. Auto Nudge parameters: threshold 1.30 mV, step 800 ns, soak 5 s, max iter 20, parallel, std dev N=8. Conditions since connect: pack 23.39→21.71 V (min 21.71), board 21.0→48.2 °C (max 48.6). Geometry: 2 bands × 11 thresholds = 22 cells; thresholds 4.7 → 0.05 V. Carried forward from cal_2x11_v5b_test: cal_2x11_v5b_test - 2026-08-13. UNTESTED, UNSWEPT. Derived on paper from cal_2x11_v5a; cells 1-4 re-targeted, cells 5-11 carried over unchanged. This is a starting point for hand-adjustment in pimd_delaycal Manual Nudge, NOT a measured profile. Do not record a corpus against it until the anchors have been nudged onto their targets on the bench.

WHY. v5a's top amplitude anchor was placed at 2.4 V when the early samples were much noisier than they are now. Bench work on 2026-08-13 in delaycal put the first cells at about 4.7 V with std dev low enough to use, so the top anchor moves 2.4 V -> 4.7 V and the ladder below it is re-cut to suit.

THE LADDER. Cell 5 is held at 125 mV - it is the tested handoff into the null region, and cells 6-8 are time-anchored and band-dependent, so moving cell 5 would move the gap into mid-descent for no gain. Anchoring both ends (4.700 V, 0.125 V) over 5 cells gives a constant step ratio of 2.4763x:
  1  4.700 V   NEW
  2  1.900 V   NEW   (geometric, 4700 * 0.40383)
  3  0.765 V   NEW   (geometric; replaces v5a's 0.500 V anchor)
  4  0.310 V   NEW   (geometric; replaces v5a's 0.250 V anchor)
  5  0.125 V   CARRIED from v5a, delay unchanged on both bands
Constant ratio because the decay is log-linear across this span, so equal voltage ratios are equal time steps. Resulting gaps: 1.368 / 1.312 / 1.192 / 1.192 us on the 100 us band and 1.320 / 1.264 / 1.144 / 1.192 us on the 10 us band - flat to within 15 %, which is the point of the re-cut.

DELAYS FOR CELLS 1-4 ARE EXTRAPOLATED, NOT MEASURED. Each was solved from v5a's own measured local decay rate in the segment bracketing the target - 0.663 / 0.741 / 0.774 / 0.760 nepers/us on the 100 us band and 0.687 / 0.770 / 0.802 / 0.753 on the 10 us band - then snapped to the 8 ns PWM grid. Cell 1 sits above the topmost v5a anchor, so its delay is an extrapolation past the end of the measured data using the 2.4 -> 1.1 V rate; the true rate is shallower at earlier times, so if it misses, cell 1 will read HIGH and wants nudging LATER.

CELLS 6-11 UNCHANGED from v5a on both bands: mid-descent, null minimum, rising out of null, and the three-point time-anchored late ladder. Their threshold_v entries are ordering keys only (see below).

HEADROOM WARNING. 4.700 V is 94 % of the 5.000 V ADC full scale. Amplitude moves 43-51 mV/V with pack state (DESIGN section 12); over the observed 19.66 -> 24.48 V pack range that is 210-245 mV, so a cold full pack could put cell 1 near 4.95 V - about 50 mV of margin before clipping. Watch cell 1 on a fresh pack; if it clips, drop the top anchor to 4.5 V and re-run the ladder.

EARLY-DELAY WARNING. On the 10 us band cell 1 lands at 7.040 us, earlier than any delay previously used on that band (v5a's shortest was 8.016 us) and earlier than the ~9-12 us window the scope captures cover. Valid in firmware terms, but unproven against the front-end transient - judge it on the std dev in delaycal.

GEOMETRY unchanged: 2 bands x 11 thresholds = 22 cells, averages 32, band frequencies and pulse widths as v5a. Different threshold_v values mean a different profile_sha8 from v5a, so frames from the two must never be mixed in one dataset (DESIGN section 10).

VALIDATED OFFLINE against the firmware's own compute_pulse_duties / pulse_duties_valid: every delay is an exact multiple of the 8 ns PWM grid, every (drive_duty, sample_duty) pair fits in 16 bits with sample strictly after drive, delays are strictly increasing and threshold_v strictly descending.

threshold_v - MIXED MEANING IN THIS PROFILE, unlike v5a where the whole column was a placeholder. Cells 1-5 carry the REAL amplitude targets in volts (4.700 / 1.900 / 0.765 / 0.310 / 0.125), which is what pimd_delaycal keys its nudge targets on. Cells 6-11 are time-anchored and band-dependent, so their entries are PLACEHOLDER ORDERING KEYS ONLY - 100 / 90 / 80 / 70 / 60 / 50 mV, chosen only to keep the column strictly descending. Do not mine cells 6-11 as voltages; the null minimum is nowhere near 80 mV on both bands (measured 59 / 69 mV).
